Born to break records, hearts, and bank accounts, the 2026 McLaren W1 hypercar is the long-awaited successor to the venerated, 903-hp P1 hybrid supercar of a decade ago. Lovingly crafted from carbon fiber and packing a 1258 horsepower hybrid powertrain, the W1 topples all of the brand's previous benchmarks: the twin-turbo V-8 and radial flux electric motor hybrid powertrain is claimed to be the most powerful in any McLaren yet; its 3084-pound dry weight calculates to a claimed power-to-weight ratio of just 2.45 pounds per horsepower. (The very, very rapid Ferrari 296 GTB hybrid , for comparison, lugs 4.3 pounds per horsepower.) Aerodynamics play their part in the W1 performance equation, of course: active aero bits including the Long Tail Rear Wing that extends rearward up to 11.8 inches combine to produce a maximum of 2205 pounds of downforce. So effective are the W1's powertrain and aero package that McLaren claims it's three seconds quicker around the company’s Nardo reference circuit than the track-focused McLaren Senna, and the W1’s 12.7-second time to 186 mph is quicker than that of the vaunted Speedtail . Remarkably and refreshingly, the W1 is a rear-wheel drive-only proposition. Record-smashing metrics aside, the new W1 is a gorgeous and exclusive work of kinetic art, the latest in a long line of road-going McLarens imbued with extraordinary levels of useable performance. If you have the means, it has the beans—to thrill beyond comprehension, that is.

Police might notice more than anyone else when crime drops off steeply. In Howard County, vehicle thefts just plummeted. According to police , lots of that drop-off comes down to kids. Interestingly, the cars in question are a part of the story too. Officers noticed that thieves appeared to focus on Kias, Hyundais, Hondas, Acuras, Chevrolets, and Dodges . These might just sound like popular brands. The reality is that, according to police, each was easy to steal thanks to key-copying programs. Now, over a dozen young people are facing serious charges.

Police counted 130 reported thefts during the second quarter (May 1-July 31) in Howard County alone. Then, in the third quarter (Aug 1-Oct 31), there were just 77 more. That's a steep decline of 53 cases in total, or around 41%. Police blame that drop on nabbing 13 young men who evidently played a large role. While they didn't all work together, their methodology was allegedly very similar.

Jaguar Land Rover has suffered a setback in its dispute with BYD over the Ti 7 SUV. Unless you only travel within driving distance of home or are willing to spend the time and money on shipping , we will all end up in a situation where renting a car is a necessity. There may be plenty of cities with fantastic public transportation systems, but you just need a car to venture out and explore the countryside. Many of us are far more care-free behind the wheel when the vehicle is owned by an abstract corporate entity and not a person with a face.

What's the worst way you've abused a rental car? I'm not talking about returning it with an empty tank. That's just a surcharge that rental companies are more than happy to add to your bill. Abuse is real, lasting damage that's an absolute nightmare to reverse. Let me use a hypothetical beach day in the South of France as an example. You and a few friends take a decent Peugeot 408 to a sleepy village on the Mediterranean. After a fun day of sand and surf, everyone piles back into the sedan right off the beach, covering the interior with sand. That's the appetizer. On the drive back, you get impatient sitting behind a truck on a two-lane road. You pull into the oncoming lane but don't get entirely clear, and you sideswipe the truck. The 408 is far worse off, with its entire right side scratched up. That's abuse!

However, I do have to come back to the rationale for the wars we as a country get into. I’m 44 years old, and it seems like we’ve been involved in wars related to oil and gas for more than half of my life. It’s just a continual process. We get into a war in the Middle East connected to XYZ, but it’s really about oil. In the middle of the 20th century, over 1,450 glaciers could be found in the contiguous U.S. Together, they covered 217 square miles (562 square kilometers) in six western states. Today, a comprehensive review my colleagues and I just published in the Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences shows their total area has shrunk by 35% and they are still shrinking, perhaps faster.
